name: Draft guest review replies for approval from Google Business Profile with SerpAPI

parameters.content:
## Draft guest review replies for approval from Google Business Profile with SerpAPI

### How it works

This workflow periodically or manually checks a Google Business Profile for recent reviews through SerpAPI, skips reviews that already have drafted replies or do not need a response, and routes new unanswered reviews by situation. It uses OpenRouter-powered AI steps to draft appropriate reply text, saves each draft to Google Sheets for approval, then sends a single email digest summarizing the drafts to review.

### Setup steps

- Configure the Schedule Trigger cadence, or use the manual trigger for testing.
- Update the property settings node with the Google Business Profile name, Google data ID, desired reply tone, and signature.
- Add SerpAPI credentials or API key configuration to the HTTP Request node that calls https://serpapi.com/search.json.
- Connect Google Sheets credentials and select the spreadsheet used to read already drafted review IDs and save new draft approvals. Clone it here https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/164ljfgREaQ_8srtrVv1LrhWMMukBdQ3mwC0KLxDylVA/edit?usp=sharing
- Configure OpenRouter credentials and model choices for the classifier and LLM draft chains.
- Connect Gmail credentials and set the approval email recipient, subject, and sender options.

### Customization

Adjust the classifier labels and the three draft prompts to match the business's review handling policy. The property tone, signature, approval sheet columns, and email digest format are also natural customization points.

## Triggers and settings

Starts the workflow either manually or on a schedule, then applies the property-specific configuration used throughout the run.

## Fetch review candidates

Loads review IDs that have already been drafted, retrieves the latest Google reviews from SerpAPI, and filters down to new unanswered reviews worth replying to.

## Route review handling

Checks whether any new reviews remain, ends cleanly when there is nothing to draft, or classifies each review into a reply situation using the nearby OpenRouter chat model.

## Generate draft replies

Creates AI-written reply drafts for reservation-check cases, disputed or possibly false reviews, and standard responses, using the shared OpenRouter model node positioned with the drafting stack.

## Combine review drafts

Merges the draft outputs from all reply paths and pairs each LLM-generated JSON draft back with the original review it answers.

## Save approval records

Writes the prepared review reply drafts into Google Sheets so they can be reviewed and approved before posting.

## Email approval digest

Builds one consolidated approval digest for the run and sends it by Gmail instead of sending one email per review.

nodes.name: Set Review and Property Info
nodes.notes:
0xd126c11a54d4ba5:0xc90af0015f0a5c3d — and that matches exactly the Black Swan data_id already on file, so this confirms it's the right one.

General steps for any property:

Open the property on Google Maps, click through until the URL has a data= parameter (searching by name sometimes gives a shorter URL without it — click the listing itself if so).
Find !1s inside that data= string.
Everything between !1s and the next ! is the data_id, always in the form 0x...:0x....
One thing to watch for: don't grab the 16s%2Fg%2F... segment further along — that's a different Google identifier (a Knowledge Graph ID), not the one SerpApi needs.

categories.description: The review includes a specific, checkable fact about the guest's reservation — a date, a room, a charge, a service, or an amenity that was supposedly included — that can't be confirmed just by reading the text and would require checking the reservation system before responding with confidence.

The review describes something that doesn't match what's known about the property, sounds like it might be about a different establishment, or includes an unusual demand or threat — reasonable grounds to doubt that it's a genuine or accurate review.
A normal review — positive, neutral, or negative — that doesn't depend on verifying a reservation and gives no reason to doubt that it's genuine.

messageValues.message: =You draft responses to guest reviews for small properties. When a review mentions a fact that depends on the reservation, you never confirm or deny it in the public reply without checking it first — you leave a clear internal note so the business can verify it. You always return a draft for a person to review before it's published.

nodes.name: Save Draft for Approval
nodes.notes: The sheet is also the memory: anything logged here is never drafted again.

messageValues.message: You draft responses to guest reviews for small properties. When a review seems fake, exaggerated, or meant for the wrong property, you never accuse the guest or argue publicly: you write a short, calm, neutral response, and save any doubts for an internal note that the business can decide what to do with. You always return a draft for a person to review before it's published.
You draft responses to guest reviews for small properties. You always return a draft for a person to review and publish. You'd rather say "this needs to be confirmed" than make up a plausible detail.
